pr_summary: Remove deprecated `dynamic=True` argument from super().__init__() calls in TensorFlow layer classes. The fix affects 4 files in the gudhi/tensorflow module: cubical_layer.py, lower_star_simplex_tree_layer.py, rips_layer.py, and perslay.py (which contains 7 layer classes). This restores compatibility with newer TensorFlow versions while preserving existing functionality.
candidate_smoke_commands: python3 -c "import gudhi.tensorflow; print('TensorFlow layers imported successfully')"
python3 -c "from gudhi.tensorflow import CubicalLayer, RipsLayer, LowerStarSimplexTreeLayer; print('Layer classes imported')"
candidate_activation_checks: python3 -c "import tensorflow as tf; print(f'TensorFlow version: {tf.__version__}')"
environment_management: The project uses CMake for building the C++ core and Python extension modules. The Python package is built using setuptools via pyproject.toml. No dedicated environment manager (conda, poetry, uv) is required, but the CI uses a custom Docker container (gudhi/pip_for_gudhi).

The fix removes dynamic=True from super().__init__() calls
perslay.py has 7 occurrences of the fix (7 different layer classes)

test_perslay.py tests all Perslay-related layer classes (GridPerslayWeight, GaussianMixturePerslayWeight, PowerPerslayWeight, GaussianPerslayPhi, TentPerslayPhi, FlatPerslayPhi, Perslay)

notes: The gudhi library is a C++ library with Python bindings for Topological Data Analysis (TDA). The TensorFlow layers module provides custom Keras layers for computing persistent homology. The fix is purely in Python code and affects TensorFlow layer initialization. The project builds with CMake and uses pip for Python packaging. Python 3.8+ is supported based on CI configuration. The tensorflow layers require TensorFlow to be installed separately. Test files test_diff.py and test_perslay.py are the primary tests for the affected code.
